A one-way ANOVA showed a significant effect of treatment group on mean resource allocation F(2,366) = 3.71, p = .03, Cohen's f = 0.14.

Planned contrasts revealed the following: (1) Participants from the two contest groups, taken together, allocated lower amounts of money (M = ¢16.91, SD = 23.94) to the recipients compared to the control group (M = ¢22.03, SD = 22.97), t(366) = -1.96, p = .05, Cohen's d = 0.22.
(2) Winners allocated marginally less to their recipients (M = ¢14.11, SD = 21.75) than did the losers (M = ¢19.75, SD = 25.76), t(366) = 1.88, p = .06, Cohen's d = 0.24.
